target.title: Add a restock endpoint
target.description: Staff can add stock to an item. require_role already rejects anonymous requests (it calls current_user), so the route doesn't also need require_login.

summary: This pull request adds a new POST endpoint at /{item_id}/restock to increase an item's quantity, protected by the @require_role("staff") decorator.

suspects.title: Missing check whether the item exists before updating
suspects.problem: The restock endpoint executes an UPDATE statement on the items table without checking if an item with the given item_id actually exists. If a non-existent ID is passed, sqlite3 UPDATE returns success with zero rows affected, and the client receives a 204 No Content response instead of a 404 Not Found.
suspects.how_to_check: Inspect other routes in app/routes/items.py, such as delete_item or update_item, to see if they query or check the existence of item_id before modifying the database, and verify what status code is expected.

arguments.suggested_fix: Check if the item exists or check the number of affected rows from db.execute, and raise HTTPError(404, "item not found") if the item does not exist.

evidence.note: restock_item executes an UPDATE statement without checking if the item exists or raising 404 when rows are not affected
other endpoints like deactivate_user check changed rows or query existence and raise 404 when not found

arguments.explanation: The restock endpoint performs an SQL UPDATE query on the items table by item_id without checking whether the item exists first. Unlike other similar modification endpoints in the application (such as deactivate_user in admin.py which checks if changed == 0 and raises a 404), restock_item returns a 204 No Content status code even when called with an invalid or non-existent item_id.
arguments.claim: The restock endpoint updates an item without verifying its existence, returning 204 No Content for non-existent items instead of 404 Not Found.
